question: Let $A=\{1,2,3\}$, $B=\{4,5,6,7\}$ and $f:A\to B$ be given by $f=\{(1,5),(2,7),(3,4)\}$. Check whether $f$ is one-one. Give reason.
explanation:
Images of domain elements
The function gives
$$f(1)=5,\quad f(2)=7,\quad f(3)=4.$$

Comparison of images
The three distinct elements $1,2,3$ have the distinct images $5,7,4$, respectively.

Conclusion
No two distinct elements of $A$ have the same image. Therefore, $f$ is one-one.

options.A: $f$ is not one-one because $6\in B$ has no pre-image
options.B: $f$ is one-one because the distinct elements $1,2,3$ have the distinct images $5,7,4$
options.C: $f$ is not one-one because $A$ and $B$ contain different numbers of elements
options.D: $f$ is one-one because every element of $B$ has a pre-image
